# Shape of the SKILL.md body · skill-authoring

Open when drafting or restructuring a SKILL.md body, or when the skill spends money or creates things outside the machine.

- **At most 500 lines** (validator fails above). Detail used only sometimes moves to `references/<topic>.md` (a file over 300 lines needs a table of contents). A file the agent must read to work correctly is linked directly from SKILL.md. A reference file may link one level further only for optional detail or skippable examples (e.g. `thai-grammar` → `thai-examples`), because Claude often does not read second-level files completely. Work a machine can do goes in `scripts/` (run without reading into context); templates go in `templates/` or `assets/`.
- Keep SKILL.md lean, because its whole body loads every time the skill opens. Heading order: `# <name> — <what it produces>` → **the one rule** in a `>` box (only if there is one) → **Use when** (2–5 concrete triggers) plus one `Not for: <case> → <other skill>` line for real look-alikes → **Steps**, numbered, each with its condition stated ("If X, do Y; otherwise Z") → **Check before done** → **References**, one line per file saying when to open it.
- Leave out of SKILL.md: lines saying which plugin it is in or that it follows `human-writing`, rules every skill already gets from the core, credits, history, motivation, and restated rules. Move to `references/`: sources with check dates (`references/sources.md`), worked examples, full templates, long option tables, per-stack detail. A hand-off rule between skills ("the agent emits an event; `async-messaging` sends it") is behaviour and stays in the steps.
- **Declare before writing**: name · target size · 3 topics that will not be covered · a table of what lives in which file, separating knowledge (constant tables) · contract (file formats) · steps. Follow [`skill-structure`](skill-structure.md).
- **Do 1 real run of the task before drafting the skill** and keep the methods that actually worked, rather than letting the AI guess (reason cited from a course clip, not measured against a baseline). An AI-written draft must pass a human reader and evals before merging. Skills are small and narrow, a few per task. SKILL.md body sits in context every turn, so write it as standing instructions; after compaction Claude Code keeps about 5,000 tokens per skill (Claude Code docs via summary, 2026-11-04). Evidence and limits: [`skill-evaluation-evidence`](skill-evaluation-evidence.md).
- **Write as a recipe saying what to do, not a prohibition.** Measured 5 runs per wording: "don't retype the value in the order form" gave an average of 4.4 retyped values, worse than no rule at all, while the recipe "copy from the source file" gave 3.0 and was stable (superpowers 2026-06 · n=5 per wording · read via summary, not reproduced yourself). "Must open before doing" rules (tripwire) work well. If 2 wordings tie, pick the shorter. Test important wording with [`eval-loop-rules`](eval-loop-rules.md). Write direct commands with a 1-line reason, no shouting in capitals. A rule about words or tone goes in first as a `before → after` pair, and becomes a rule once it repeats twice (`learn-loop/session-lessons-to-skills` item 2).
- A new item that contradicts an old one → fix the old one, do not append. A skill that continues work from another names that skill and section instead of copying its content (example: `human-writing/translate-th-en` points to `thai-grammar` section 7).
- Numbers that change over time (prices · rules · versions) carry the date checked, and go into `scripts/check/facts.json` if you want the validator to warn when stale.
- **A skill that costs money or creates things outside the machine** (renting cloud machines · GPU · purchases · APIs billed per call) needs all 4: (1) a money ceiling set by the user; the skill cannot raise it itself and must ask first (2) never delete or cancel the user's own things without asking (3) after deleting, re-check with a list command that they are really gone, then summarise the actual cost (4) say clearly that stop is not destroy, because a merely stopped item still bills for storage. Pair with `disable-model-invocation: true` when the model should not call it itself. Use the least-privilege key that is enough (e.g. no billing-edit rights) and check the environment by reporting only OK or MISSING, never printing the value (pattern from the course's VastAi_Skill lab, CWN2026).
  - GPU rental example from the course (numbers from a single run, not a standard): download cost per GB can exceed the GPU cost (11.8 GB × $0.029 = $0.34 vs GPU $0.16), so set a `inet_down_cost` ceiling when choosing a machine. Advertised network speed cannot be trusted (advertised 1391 Mbps, actual 1.8 MB/s): measure, then switch machines. The invoice total keeps growing after destroy: wait until it settles before summarising costs.
